newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower on profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open marginally lower Monday as small marketers took advantage of some profits, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.24 to $2.26 after settling to the upside Friday at $2.267 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
"It appears we're getting a little profit taking here," one source said, noting early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked steady at $2.18-2.21 per mmBtu.

Although support in June was pegged at $2.20, many traders doubted the contract's ability to break through that level. Further support was seen at $2.17, and then at $2.05 and along the up trendline at $2.01. Resistance was pegged at $2.33 and then at the $2.385 contract high.
In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly at $2.15-20. Midcon pipes were off a couple of cents to about $2. New York city gate gas was talked again on either side of $2.45.

Temperatures throughout most of the Northeast and upper Midwest are forecast to hover near to slightly below normal this week. Warmer-than-normal weather in the Southeast should lead to an increase in air conditioning demand among those customers.
